newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Samsung Corp to start refining gold.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Samsung Corp to start refining gold.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Corp, a unit of Samsung Group, will start refining gold next week in a tie-up with German firm Heraeus Oriental Hitec Co Ltd, a Heraeus official said on Tuesday.

Production will get under way in a plant in South Korea's western port city of Inchon, Won Kang-hee, a Seoul-based manager of Heraeus Oriental Hitec, told Reuters. The plant has an annual capacity of 30 tonnes of refined gold bars.
Won said Samsung would import low grade gold of 99.5 percent purity to turn into gold bars with more than 99.99 percent purity.
He said the factory was scheduled to operate at full capacity starting next month. Output would be marketed by Samsung under the Heraeus brand name.
Heraeus gold is listed on the London Bullion Market Association.
Heraeus Oriental is wholly-owned by Germany's W.C. Heraeus Gmbh, which produces gold bonding wire and potassium gold cyanide, according to Won.

Won said under the tie-up, Heraeus provided land for the Inchon plant and technical expertise. Samsung supplied plant and equipment and would market the production. He gave no details of the size of the investment.
Heraeus Oriental would take some of the output to manufacture gold bonding wire at a plant in South Korea, Won said. The wire would be sold to Samsung Electronics Co Ltd .
Heraeus buys about five tonnes of gold each year for wire production in South Korea, Won said.
Samsung officials were not available for comment.

Traders said one attraction for Samsung Corp in gold refining was that it would enable the company to get around rules aimed at curbing a once booming gold transhipment business by South Korean bullion houses.
The rules, introduced last July, shortened to 30 days from 120 days the deferred payment period for gold imports.

Previously, bullion houses had imported huge quanties of gold on deferred payment, immediately exported the metal and parked the proceeds on the domestic money market to take advantage of high interest rates in South Korea.
Gold imported for refining is still subject to the old 120-day deferred payment rule.
If the gold is then exported, there is a three percent import tax rebate.
LG Metals Corp and Korea Zinc Co Ltd are currently the largest gold refiners in South Korea.
